_comment: The cut list, as data. Re-derive against a new source with tools/recut.py.
source_note: Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ep.04 'Kill The Shadow', 1920x1080 23.976. The Bankai runs 784.30-805.76s (13:04-13:26). Cut points came from tools/probe_cuts.py scene detection, not by eye.
crop_note: The source is already 1920x1080 16:9, so no shot is cropped or scaled: every plate is the original pixels 1:1. The panel this plays on is 1920x1080, so that is also the delivery size.
watermark: animepahe logo, alpha-composited top-left. Removed by inverting the blend -- see tools/dewatermark.py.

shots.name: shot01_release
shots.beat: the hand opens and lets the sword fall

shots.name: shot02_sink
shots.beat: the blade touches stone and rings out in circles

shots.name: shot03_bankai
shots.beat: black; a small figure; the blade rows rise into wings

shots.name: shot04_declare
shots.reframe_why: the burned-in 'Senbonzakura Kageyoshi...' subtitle sits on rows 968-1048, on his moving haori, so there is no clean plate to borrow from. Cropping above it and pushing in 1.125x removes it with no invented pixels, and tightens the close-up while it is at it.

shots.name: shot05_firstjet
shots.beat: one jet of petals breaks upward

shots.name: shot09_stand
shots.beat: he stands inside it; the hold the login lands on

detext.why: the 'Bankai...' subtitle. This shot is a held near-black frame -- frames 13 and 37 differ by 0.53 DN over the whole picture -- so the covered region can be rebuilt exactly from the frames either side instead of being inpainted.

pipeline: tools/recut.py runs: cut (native, no scaling) -> dewatermark -> reframe -> detext -> assemble
dewatermark must precede reframe: the logo calibration is tied to its position in the untouched frame
